survivingNew.title: Pre-migration the derived Referrer set is empty, so D6 (no agent loses a skill) is unimplementable from the Contract as written
survivingNew.problem: The Contract calls the union of held-links + native-readers 'the authoritative set', and defines the held-links arm as 'agent dirs whose <dir>/<name> is a link resolving to the Master' — where Master is now .aghub/<name>. On an un-migrated host .aghub/<name> does not exist, so nothing resolves to it and that arm yields the empty set. Migration derives its Referrer worklist (D6) from the same section, so it would relink only the native readers of .agents/skills and drop every per-agent link (claude, grok, ... — the majority). D6 promises exactly the opposite. The seam the spec cites proves the point itself: universal_relink_referrers' doc says 'MUST be called BEFORE the master is renamed (the per-link canonicalize resolves through the still-present master)' — it is an OLD-master query, and the spec cites it as a NEW-master query.
survivingNew.evidence: crates/core/src/manager/skill.rs:1449 filter is 'Linker::is_link(&link) && fs::canonicalize(&link).map(|r| r == *old_real).unwrap_or(false)'. Fixture J (scratchpad probe.rs, case J): a legacy host with .agents/skills/foo a real dir and .grok/skills/foo a symlink to it, M = .aghub/foo missing. canonicalize(R) resolves to .agents/skills/foo, canonicalize(M) is Err, so the membership test is false — grok is not in the set. Ran it: the per-agent referrer scores c2_both_ok=false, i.e. excluded.
survivingNew.fix: State in the Contract that there are TWO derivations, not one: migration derives its Referrer worklist against the OLD master path (.agents/skills/<name>, the value universal_relink_referrers was written for), while verify_shape derives against the new Master. One sentence, but without it the migration section and D6 contradict each other.
survivingNew.target: Revision 2 of .scratch/aghub-skill-store/spec.md, the conformant(R, M) predicate and the four-shapes table in the Contract section (spec lines 80-143)
survivingNew.reviewer_note: Confirmed at source and by fixture. crates/core/src/manager/skill.rs:1449-1465 is exactly the filter quoted, and its own doc at :1447-1448 reads 'MUST be called BEFORE the master is renamed (the per-link canonicalize resolves through the still-present master)' - an OLD-master query, cited by spec line 103-105 as a NEW-master query. I reproduced case J (legacy host: .agents/skills/foo a real dir, .grok/skills/foo a symlink to it, .aghub/foo absent): the membership test is_link(R) and canonicalize(R)==canonicalize(M) evaluates false, so grok is excluded. With M absent nothing can resolve to it, so the held-links arm yields the empty set on every un-migrated host - which is the only host migration ever runs on. D6 promises no agent loses a skill it can read now; the Contract as written hands migration a worklist that contains none of the per-agent link holders. Not a duplicate of attack finding 6 (which killed the lock-recorded set); this is a defect introduced by revision 2's replacement.
survivingNew.corrected_fix: Two derivations, stated separately in the Contract. Migration-time: derive against the OLD master path (~/.agents/skills or root/.agents/skills), the value universal_relink_referrers was written for, and fix that list BEFORE the master moves. Steady state: derive against the new Master. Say which one each consumer uses. See also verdict 28 - the single derivation that actually answers both is classify_paths against the NEW Master, with the migration-time list a one-shot separate query.

survivingNew.title: conformant() is circular: for per-agent Referrers the set membership test IS clauses 1 and 2, so only clause 3 can ever fire
survivingNew.problem: The held-links arm admits a path only if it is a link AND it canonicalizes to the Master. Those are precisely clause 1 and clause 2 of conformant(). So for every per-agent Referrer the predicate can only ever fail on clause 3 (the chain check); a dangling per-agent link, a link pointing at a foreign target, and a real directory left by npx add are not reported as violations — they are silently absent from the set. The spec's 'Detection is bounded' section concedes only that a MISSING per-agent Referrer is undetectable. The true bound is much wider: the entire non-conformant, non-chain class is undetectable for per-agent Referrers. Policy 1's motivating case survives only because the native-readers arm contributes the fixed shared-slot path, whose shape is unconstrained.
survivingNew.evidence: Same filter at crates/core/src/manager/skill.rs:1449. Fixture C2 (dangling R with M present) and fixture J (R pointing at .agents/skills) both score violation under every fold — but both would be excluded from the set before the predicate ever runs. Fixture E-prime (the shared slot itself) is reachable only through the native-readers arm.
survivingNew.fix: Rewrite the 'Detection is bounded' paragraph to say: for per-agent Referrers conformant() reduces to clause 3, because the derivation already asserts clauses 1 and 2. If broken per-agent links must be reported, the held-links arm needs a second, weaker query — every agent skills dir in scope whose <dir>/<name> exists at all — and the spec must name where that query lives.

survivingNew.title: The predicate does not compile, and the only obvious Err-fold certifies a dangling Referrer as healthy
survivingNew.problem: Clause 2 is written as canonicalize(R) == canonicalize(M). io::Error does not implement PartialEq, so that expression is rejected by rustc — the predicate is pseudocode whose Err semantics are undefined, and clause 3 additionally carries a bare question-mark operator with no statement of what the caller does with the Err. The natural fold, comparing the two Options, makes two Errs compare EQUAL. That is the exact rule the spec itself lays down for the Policy-2 tri-state ('two Errs must never compare equal'), broken by its own predicate. Concretely: R dangling and M missing scores is_link=true, clause2 true (None equals None), clause3 Err-treated-as-pass — CONFORMANT. Reachable shape: a user removes the .aghub store after migration, so every Referrer dangles and every M is gone; the legacy arm needs a real directory so it does not fire, and apply-update or source sync then proceeds against a store it believes is healthy.
survivingNew.evidence: literal.rs in the scratchpad fails to compile with E0369, 'binary operation == cannot be applied to type Result<PathBuf, std::io::Error>', note: std::io::Error does not implement PartialEq. probe.rs case C prints is_link=true c2_ok_eq=true c2_both_ok=false c3_strict=false c3_lenient=true, VERDICT loose-fold=CONFORMANT strict-fold=violation. Case C2 (dangling with M present) is a violation under both folds, so the danger is specific to M also being absent.
survivingNew.fix: Spell the predicate with explicit Ok requirements: clause 2 must be 'both canonicalize calls return Ok AND the values are equal'; clause 3 must be 'symlink_metadata returns Ok AND the type is not a symlink'. Say in the text that any Err on either clause is a violation, never a pass, and cite the same two-Errs rule already stated for the hash tri-state.
survivingNew.target: Revision 2 of .scratch/aghub-skill-store/spec.md, the conformant(R, M) predicate and the four-shapes table in the Contract section (spec lines 80-143)

I did reproduce E0369 ('binary operation == cannot be applied to type Result<PathBuf, std::io::Error>', note: std::io::Error does not implement PartialEq), which is why the Err semantics genuinely are undefined rather than merely unwritten. The failure is real and I ran it: case C (R dangling, M absent) scores is_link=true, Option-fold clause 2 true (None equals None), clause 3 lenient pass, verdict CONFORMANT; under the strict fold it is a violation. Any Err on any clause is a violation, never a pass. Cite the same two-Errs rule already written for the hash tri-state so the two sections agree.

survivingNew.title: Table order and the 'Identity before hash, always' rule contradict each other, and the two sanctioned identity checks disagree on absent paths
survivingNew.problem: The four-shapes table would classify a missing Referrer as 'absent' (legal). The 'Identity before hash' section says any comparison that can lead to a deletion runs the identity check FIRST, using resolve_existing or dev plus ino. When .agents/skills is a symlink into the store (the stow shape the spec itself introduces) and the skill is simply not installed, resolve_existing returns the same path for R and M even though neither exists, and is_link(R) is false — so aliased-master fires and the command refuses, on a skill that is not there. The two sanctioned methods also disagree: dev plus ino cannot be computed for a non-existent path at all, while resolve_existing happily reports equality. One rule, two methods, opposite answers.
survivingNew.evidence: probe.rs case K: .agents/skills is a symlink to ../.aghub, .aghub exists, .aghub/foo and the Referrer leaf both missing. Output: is_link=false, c2_ok_eq=true, c2_both_ok=false, lenient_eq=true, resolve_eq=true, and both ALIASED-MASTER lines fire (plain canonicalize and canonicalize_lenient). dev plus ino would require a stat of a path that does not exist.
survivingNew.fix: Say explicitly that the absent arm is evaluated before the identity check, and that the identity check applies only when BOTH sides exist. Pick one identity method rather than offering two; if resolve_existing is kept, add the existence precondition in the same sentence.
survivingNew.target: Revision 2 of .scratch/aghub-skill-store/spec.md, the conformant(R, M) predicate and the four-shapes table in the Contract section (spec lines 80-143)
survivingNew.reviewer_note: Half of it overreaches, half survives. The overreach: spec line 157 scopes the rule to 'any comparison that can lead to a deletion', and an absent Referrer leads to no deletion, so the claimed false refusal on a not-installed skill requires reading the rule more broadly than it is written. The surviving half is real and I confirmed it: case K (.agents/skills a symlink to ../.aghub, .aghub present, both leaves absent) gives canonicalize(R)=Err and canonicalize(M)=Err, so the Option fold reports equal and the aliased-master arm fires with is_link(R)=false; resolve_existing (crates/skill/src/lock/guard.rs:154, longest-existing-prefix) returns the identical path for both sides; and dev plus ino cannot be computed for a path that does not exist at all. The spec offers two methods in one sentence and they answer differently on non-existent paths. Same root as verdict 5.
survivingNew.corrected_fix: One sentence: the identity check applies only when both sides exist, and it is evaluated after the absent arm. Pick ONE method - resolve_existing, since dev plus ino cannot answer for a non-existent path and would need the same precondition anyway - and drop the 'or' from spec line 158.

survivingNew.title: Four different path normalizers decide one question, and they disagree on the exact inputs the spec is about
survivingNew.problem: The Contract's predicate uses plain canonicalize; the identity check one section later uses resolve_existing or dev plus ino; read_effect_after — which the Removal section keeps as the single verdict — uses canonicalize_lenient throughout, including via entry_identity, which is itself the parent-plus-file-name walk root AGENTS.md bans by name. These are not interchangeable on non-existent or partly-aliased paths, and the spec never says which one verify_shape must use. Mixing them means a shape can be a violation to the predicate and healthy to the removal verdict for the same skill in the same command.
survivingNew.evidence: probe.rs prints all three per case. Case C (dangling R, missing M): plain canonicalize gives Err/Err (equal under the Option fold), canonicalize_lenient gives NOT equal, resolve_existing gives NOT equal. Case K (aliased dir, both leaves missing): plain canonicalize Err/Err, canonicalize_lenient EQUAL, resolve_existing EQUAL. Source: crates/core/src/skills/linker/classify.rs:82, crates/skill/src/lock/guard.rs:154, crates/core/src/skills/removal.rs:253 and :419.
survivingNew.fix: Name one normalizer for verify_shape in the Contract and state why the other two are not it — plain canonicalize because it is the only one that refuses to invent a value for a path that does not exist, which is what a shape check needs. Add a line that entry_identity and canonicalize_lenient keep their existing role in read_effect_after and are not the shape check.
survivingNew.target: Revision 2 of .scratch/aghub-skill-store/spec.md, the conformant(R, M) predicate and the four-shapes table in the Contract section (spec lines 80-143)
survivingNew.reviewer_note: Citations check out and the disagreement is real. crates/core/src/skills/linker/classify.rs:82 canonicalize_lenient (canonicalize, else longest existing ancestor plus lexical tail); crates/skill/src/lock/guard.rs:154 resolve_existing; crates/core/src/skills/removal.rs:250-258 entry_identity and :419 canonicalize_lenient inside read_effect_after. The Contract's predicate uses plain canonicalize; the identity rule one section later names resolve_existing or dev plus ino; read_effect_after - which spec line 208 keeps as the single removal verdict - uses neither. My fixtures show them splitting on exactly the spec's own inputs: case C plain canonicalize gives Err/Err (equal under the Option fold) while the lenient and resolve_existing forms are NOT equal; case K plain gives Err/Err while lenient and resolve_existing are EQUAL. So one shape can be a violation to the predicate and healthy to the removal verdict in the same command. One overreach: entry_identity is not the parent/file_name walk AGENTS.md bans - it resolves the parent and deliberately does not resolve the leaf, and removal.rs:245-249 says why. Drop that clause.
survivingNew.corrected_fix: Name plain canonicalize as verify_shape's normalizer in the Contract, with the reason: it is the only one that refuses to invent a value for a path that does not exist, which is what a shape check needs. Add one line saying canonicalize_lenient and entry_identity keep their existing roles inside read_effect_after and are not the shape check, and that resolve_existing is the identity check's normalizer (verdict 4). Do not repeat the claim that entry_identity violates the AGENTS.md ban.

survivingNew.title: Clause 3 is leaf-only, so a Referrer routed through the shared slot certifies as conformant, and per-Referrer verdicts have no stated aggregation
survivingNew.problem: Clause 3 lstats the one-hop target and asks whether that final component is a symlink. When the symlink hop lives in the PATH PREFIX rather than the leaf — the stow shape where .agents/skills is itself a directory symlink into the store — the lstat walks through the symlinked prefix and lands on a real directory, so the chain is not detected. The Referrer is then certified healthy even though it reads through .agents/skills, which is exactly the surface npx add rewrites. The spec never says whether a Referrer routed through the shared slot is conformant, and it never says how the per-Referrer verdicts combine into the single per-skill refusal verify_shape returns.
survivingNew.evidence: probe.rs case E: .agents/skills is a symlink to ../.aghub, R at .grok/skills/foo targets ../../.agents/skills/foo, master at .aghub/foo. Output: is_link=true c2_both_ok=true c3_strict=true, VERDICT CONFORMANT under both folds. The mitigating fact is case E-prime in the same scope: the shared slot itself scores aliased-master, so the skill is refused via the other Referrer — if and only if the aggregation is 'any violation refuses'.
survivingNew.fix: Two sentences in the Contract: say clause 3 tests the leaf only and that a prefix symlink is deliberately out of scope because the aliased-master arm on the shared slot covers the same host; and state the aggregation rule explicitly — one non-conformant Referrer refuses the whole skill.

survivingNew.reviewer_note: Both halves reproduce. Case E (.agents/skills a directory symlink to ../.aghub, .grok/skills/foo targeting ../../.agents/skills/foo, master at .aghub/foo) scores is_link=true, both-Ok clause 2 true, clause 3 true - CONFORMANT under both folds, even though the Referrer reads through the surface npx add rewrites. survivingNew.title: Clause 3 makes a symlinked master leaf a violation, which the spec never addresses
survivingNew.problem: The spec covers the store directory being a symlink (a user pointing .aghub elsewhere) and that case passes. It does not cover a single skill inside the store being a symlink — a user linking .aghub/foo at a checkout they edit in place, the same habit the source-authoring flow encourages. Clause 3 lstats the one-hop target, which for a healthy Referrer IS the master leaf, so a symlinked master leaf reads as a chain and the skill is refused with a chain diagnosis that names the wrong problem.
survivingNew.evidence: probe.rs case I: .aghub/foo is a symlink to ../elsewhere/foo, R targets ../../.aghub/foo. Output: is_link=true c2_both_ok=true c3_strict=false, VERDICT violation under both folds — the same score as the genuine npx two-hop chain in case D, so the two are indistinguishable to the caller. Case H (.aghub itself a symlink) is CONFORMANT, confirming the asymmetry is at the leaf.
survivingNew.fix: Add a row to the four-shapes table, or one sentence saying a symlinked master leaf is a violation on purpose and the message must name the master, not the Referrer, so the user is not told to fix the wrong link.

survivingNew.title: On Windows, clause 1 and clause 3 use different link definitions, so a cloud-placeholder directory can miss the legacy arm
survivingNew.problem: Linker::is_link returns true for ANY reparse point, testing FILE_ATTRIBUTE_REPARSE_POINT after the is_symlink check. Rust's own is_symlink on Windows is true for name-surrogate tags only — symlinks and junctions. Clause 1 therefore accepts tags clause 3 rejects: OneDrive Files-On-Demand placeholders, dedup stubs, AppExecLink. For those, read_link returns Err (not a supported reparse point), so clause 3 has nothing to test, and the legacy arm — which requires a real directory — will not fire either if it is expressed as not-is_link. A project-scope .agents/skills under a OneDrive-synced folder is the reachable case; the global path under the user profile usually is not. Junctions themselves are fine: read_link returns an absolute target and Path::join replaces the base, and is_symlink is true for junctions so a junction second hop IS caught.
survivingNew.evidence: crates/core/src/skills/linker/mod.rs:303-318 shows the extra FILE_ATTRIBUTE_REPARSE_POINT branch beyond is_symlink. Reasoned from that source plus Rust's documented Windows is_symlink semantics; NOT run — this session is Linux only. The absolute-target half of the claim IS verified on Linux (probe.rs case B).
survivingNew.fix: State which is_link the predicate uses and require the same definition in all three clauses, or make the legacy arm test is_dir positively rather than not-is_link. Also say what a read_link Err means for clause 3 on Windows — currently unstated, and it is not the same situation as a dangling link.
survivingNew.target: Revision 2 of .scratch/aghub-skill-store/spec.md, the conformant(R, M) predicate and the four-shapes table in the Contract section (spec lines 80-143)
survivingNew.reviewer_note: The source half is exact and I read it: crates/core/src/skills/linker/mod.rs:303-318 returns true on file_type().is_symlink() and then, under cfg(windows), also on FILE_ATTRIBUTE_REPARSE_POINT (0x0400) - strictly wider than Rust's is_symlink, which on Windows covers name-surrogate tags only. So clause 1 can accept a reparse point for which read_link returns Err and clause 3 has nothing to test, while a legacy arm expressed as not-is_link also will not fire. The finding is honest that it could not run this (Linux-only session) and it verified the absolute-target half on Linux. It is a real unstated case, not a demonstrated failure, and the reachable path (a project-scope .agents/skills under a OneDrive-synced folder) is narrow - the repo already accepts a Windows clippy-only gap (root AGENTS.md).
survivingNew.corrected_fix: State which is_link the predicate uses and require the same definition in all three clauses, and say what a read_link Err means for clause 3 - it is not the same situation as a dangling link. Simplest: make the legacy arm test is_dir positively rather than not-is_link, so an unsupported reparse point cannot fall between the two arms.

survivingNew.title: Equal-branch repair is not transactional; a dead repair is indistinguishable from a deliberate withhold
survivingNew.problem: The spec makes migration transactional but says nothing about repair. The Equal branch is rename fork to quarantine, then create the Referrer symlink. Between those two steps the skill is readable from NOWHERE by any agent using that slot. Anything that ends the process there — SIGKILL, Ctrl-C, ENOSPC, a read-only or EACCES .agents/skills, a Windows host where both symlink_dir and the mklink /J junction fallback fail (crates/core/src/skills/linker/mod.rs:504-515, network drive or non-NTFS) — leaves Master present, Referrer absent. Per the spec's own four-shapes table that is the LEGAL absent shape, meaning 'not granted to that agent'. So nothing reports it: doctor's row is health ok (the Master is fine, health only looks at the Master), and the migration receipt — the mechanism invented precisely to disambiguate absent — is a migration-only artifact. The content is sitting in a directory nothing lists. The spec also bans copy-on-symlink-failure, so there is no degraded mode. There is a second horn: today AgentLinkState::Missing IS an issue (doctor.rs:107-119). The withhold feature forces Missing to become non-issue, or doctor goes red for every agent a user deliberately withheld from. Either choice makes a died repair silent.
survivingNew.evidence: Reasoned from crates/core/src/skills/linker/mod.rs:489-515 (create_link error paths), doctor.rs:107-119 (AgentLinkState::is_issue), doctor.rs:361-371 (health_of ignores Referrers), and the spec's own four-shapes table plus its 'Emits a receipt' paragraph, which scopes the receipt to migration only. Not executed.
survivingNew.fix: Reorder so no rollback is needed: create the Referrer symlink at a temp name inside the slot directory FIRST (this proves link creation works on this filesystem and platform before anything destructive), then rename fork to quarantine, then rename the temp link over <name>. The whole ENOSPC / EACCES / no-symlink-privilege class then fails before any move. Only a SIGKILL between the two renames remains, and both leftovers are self-describing markers. Then make the quarantine itself the receipt by layering it as .quarantine/<name>/<stamp>/ rather than the flat <name>-<stamp> (sanitized names contain hyphens, so the flat form cannot be split back): doctor can then decide that a quarantine for <name> plus an absent slot means the repair died, versus a conformant slot meaning ordinary leftover. Decidable with no sidecar, still one level deep for prune.

survivingNew.title: Undecidable(HashError) has no exit — some causes are permanent and deterministic
survivingNew.problem: Undecidable routes to refuse-and-disclose, and verify_shape refuses the skills the command NAMES — including a delete of the very skill that is stuck. The spec offers no escape. Several HashError causes are permanent, not transient: HashError::Bounds is fully deterministic (crates/skill/src/hash.rs:13-15 — MAX_FILES 10000, MAX_TOTAL_BYTES 256 MiB, MAX_DEPTH 64), so a large fork is Undecidable on every retry even when it is byte-identical to the Master; and HashError::Io from EACCES on a root-owned file inside the fork (a user who ran sudo npx skills add) never clears while running as that user. Both put the user in a state where every aghub verb for that skill refuses and the only way out is a manual recursive delete of the fork — precisely the blind destructive act the whole policy is built to avoid. Worse, Bounds is asymmetric to the risk: it fires on exactly the fat forks (large assets) where an accidental deletion costs most.
survivingNew.evidence: Read crates/skill/src/hash.rs:13-15 (bounds constants), :42-70 (collect and update_hasher_from_file propagate every io::Error), :22-27 (HashError has exactly Io and Bounds). Confirmed collect skips symlinks and .git/node_modules but counts everything else toward the byte budget. Not executed.
survivingNew.fix: No force flag needed — the escape hatch is already a verb. delete does not need the comparison at all: the user's stated intent is removal, and quarantine-by-rename is strictly safer than the recursive delete a stuck user performs by hand. So delete of a real-directory fork should quarantine unconditionally and report it, while add / apply-update / source sync keep refusing on Undecidable. Also disclose in the refusal WHICH cause fired (bounds versus io) so the user knows retrying is pointless.

survivingNew.title: <stamp> is unspecified and a same-instant collision is a hard error mid-repair
survivingNew.problem: The spec writes .aghub/.quarantine/<name>-<stamp>/ but never says where <stamp> comes from. If it is second-resolution (the obvious choice) two repairs of the same skill in the same second collide, and rename onto an existing non-empty directory fails. It is reachable in practice: a scripted loop, or a multi-agent fan-out that repairs the same shared slot once per named agent. tempfile is NOT available as a production dependency of aghub-core (crates/core/Cargo.toml:16 marks it optional behind the testing feature, :24 is dev-dependencies), so the usual collision-free helper cannot be reached for here.
survivingNew.evidence: Ran fs::rename of a non-empty directory onto another non-empty directory: Os { code: 39, kind: DirectoryNotEmpty }. Confirmed rename onto an EMPTY directory succeeds, so a partially created stamp directory would silently absorb the move. Checked crates/core/Cargo.toml for tempfile.
survivingNew.fix: Specify it, and make collision impossible rather than unlikely: with the .quarantine/<name>/<stamp>/ layout from the transaction fix, use a UTC timestamp to nanosecond resolution plus a bounded retry that appends -2, -3 on AlreadyExists. Never create the stamp directory before the rename — rename into a pre-created empty directory succeeds and would mask a collision instead of failing it.

survivingNew.title: Cross-filesystem rename (EXDEV) and Windows sharing violations have no specified fallback
survivingNew.problem: The rename moves .agents/skills/<name> into .aghub/.quarantine. The spec assumes one filesystem. Both scopes can break that, and the spec's own text supplies the case: its aliased-master section documents .agents/skills being a symlink (stow, or a hand-fixed layout). If that symlink points at a dotfiles repo on another mount, a container bind mount, or an external volume, the rename returns EXDEV. Project scope adds devcontainer and bind-mount layouts where <root>/.agents is mounted separately from <root>. On Windows there is a second class: renaming a directory tree fails with a sharing violation while any file inside has an open handle — an agent process reading SKILL.md is enough. The danger is not the failure, it is the fallback an implementer will reach for: copy the tree then recursively delete the source, which reintroduces exactly the remove_dir_all the policy bans, on content the hash already proved is not the whole story.
survivingNew.evidence: Reasoned from the spec's own aliased-master paragraph (which establishes a symlinked .agents/skills as an in-scope layout) and from std::fs::rename semantics. Not executed — I have no cross-mount fixture here.
survivingNew.fix: State it explicitly: on any rename error the repair REFUSES, names both absolute paths and the errno, and changes nothing. Never fall back to copy plus recursive delete. Say so in the spec text next to the remove_dir_all ban, because that is the fallback a reviewer will otherwise wave through as obviously safe.

survivingNew.title: Quarantine grows without bound and no aghub verb ever lists or reaps it
survivingNew.problem: Every npx add / install / update / check forks the content (the spec's own table), and every subsequent aghub repair quarantines a full copy. Nothing removes them. prune-lock cannot see them (correctly — top_level_skill_dirs requires a root SKILL.md). No CLI verb enumerates them. Sizes are not small: the spec's own argument for keeping them is that a fork can exclusively hold a .git tree, a node_modules tree, symlinks and empty directories — the fat cases. So a user alternating between the two tools accumulates one full copy per skill per repair, silently, inside their home directory or their repository root, with no aghub command that even names the directory. The one surface that DOES show it is doctor, and it shows it wrongly (finding 1).
survivingNew.evidence: Reasoned from the spec's Policy 2 text plus prune.rs:464-481 (quarantine correctly excluded) and the absence of any other store enumerator; confirmed by grepping for callers of top_level_skill_dirs, entry_paths and load_skills_from_dir_partial across crates/.
survivingNew.fix: Fold into finding 1's fix rather than adding machinery: the quarantined doctor row reports name, stamp and size, and prune-lock or a doctor flag offers to drop quarantines older than a stated retention (30 days is a defensible default). One row plus one opt-in reap; no new command, no background job.

judge.q1_decision:
不新增任何授權持久化(無 sidecar、無 grants 檔、無 receipt 檔)。骨幹取 minimal-diff:崩潰安全靠「順序 + 可重跑的冪等 migration」,不靠紀錄。

載重順序(migration 每個 skill):先 copy 出 .aghub/<n> → 再建每個有私有目錄的 agent 的 Referrer → 最後才換共用槽位(先建暫時 link .agents/skills/.<n>.aghub-migrating,再把舊實體目錄 rename 進 .aghub/.quarantine/,再 rename 暫時 link 蓋上 <n>)。POSIX 不允許 symlink rename 覆蓋非空目錄,這個暫時名是唯一能把窗口收到零的做法,且它是 transient,resume 時 unlink。

任何時點死掉留下的只有兩種:舊實體目錄仍在服務(等於 legacy,無人失去技能),或「M 存在 + R 是實體目錄」——後者正好就是 npx add 的形狀,直接吃既有 Policy 2 修復(tri-state:Equal→quarantine 後補 link;Diverged/Undecidable→拒絕並揭露)。所以不需要第五個 shape。

doctor 的第三個休息態不新增 variant:AgentLinkState::Missing 在「lock 有 + Master 在 + 該 agent 無 Referrer」時改名 Withheld、is_issue=false。orphanMaster 不動(已驗證 gate 已是 !tracked)。

接受的代價要寫進文件:使用者手動 rm 掉 Referrer 永遠等同「從未授權」,沒有 restore-my-grants,沒有稽核軌跡。
judge.q1_rejected:
否決 surface-first 的 .aghub/.grants.json:(1) 它是第二個真相來源,和推導出來的磁碟現況天生會分岔,而提案自己承認 Mac 與 VM、還原備份、手動遷移過的主機永遠停在 unrecorded——等於用一個新狀態換掉一個舊的不可判定;(2) grant-broken 會對「使用者自己整理 link」與 npx 之外的任何外力發假警報,而 doctor 一旦會誤報,使用者就學會忽略它,這比不報更糟;(3) project scope 的檔案會落在使用者 repo 根,和尚未決定的 .gitignore 綁死;(4) 新增持久化狀態才有的失效模式(壞檔、部分寫入、跨主機)全部是我們自找的,而它唯一買到的能力是「區分手動刪 link 與從未授權」,那不是任何指令的輸入。

否決 type-first 的 .aghub/.migrating/<n> marker 與第五個 Interrupted shape:它把一個「順序就能消滅的窗口」升級成一個新的持久檔 + 新形狀 + 一個沒有 TTL、SIGKILL 後會卡住整個 skill 直到人工介入的狀態(提案自己承認 apply-update 在那之前都會失敗)。我們的順序讓每個崩潰窗口要嘛無害、要嘛落進既有的 npx 修復路徑,不需要新概念。

同時否決 surface-first 對 orphanMaster 的重新定義:已驗證 doctor.rs 的 OrphanMaster 需要 !tracked,spec 的「會把 happy path 報成故障」是錯的。
judge.q2_decision:
不在 LinkNeed 上加任何欄位,不新增 shared_slots 表。共用性只有一個 oracle:既有且已 pub 的 removal::skill_dir_readers_outside(dir, scope, root, requested)——它的 doc 早就把「指名全部讀者是合法的、只指名一部分才危險」寫成政策,API delete 路由也已在用。

改動:
1. 刪 LinkNeed::NativeReader(變更後沒有 agent 讀 .aghub,它必然不可達;刪掉才會讓編譯器把每個 match 站點列出來)。同時刪 doctor 的 AutoCovered。
2. 把 NeedsLink 的欄位 agent_skills_dir 改名 referrer_dir 並改寫那句 "private" 的謊。改名是免費的編譯器掃描,強迫每個 consumer 看一次現場——這是 Slot enum 想要的效果的便宜版。

4. coverage wire:拿掉 reads_master / writes_master / auto_covered(變更後恆假),換成 shared_with: Vec<String>,只在 classify_all 填(那條路徑本來就付全 roster 成本)。刪欄位是編譯器 + ts-rs 強制的,desktop 現成但沒人 render 的 i18n 字串正好接上。
5. 三個已驗證的安裝修正:symlink_dirs 去重;把 already_linked 的 parent 併進「歸屬」集合(created_referrer_dirs 維持只取 install.linked,那是 rollback 收據);回傳前 assert agent_results.len() == target_agents.len()。

拒絕,但不新增旗標、不新增 outcome、不新增 refusal code——用既有的 kept/refuse 契約。

放在 remove_skill_planned(不是 plan_removal:rename.rs 有兩個呼叫點,不能被擋),就在 plan_removal 與 read_effect_after 之間,scope/project_root/requested 都已在手。新 helper 放 removal.rs,緊鄰 single_agent_keep_reason。

判準用「真的會失去的人」,不是「誰讀得到這個目錄」:對 skill_dir_readers_outside 回傳的每個未被指名 agent,用該 agent 自己的讀路徑再問一次 read_effect_after。這是必要的精修——codex 若已有私有 Referrer,共用槽位被拿掉它一樣讀得到(canonicalize 後 before==after,changed=false),不該擋;只有 changed=true 的才是受害者。判準仍只有一個家。

judge.q4_decision:
刪掉 SkillCapabilities.universal。骨幹取 minimal-diff 的機械清單,但拿掉它的 XDG 寫入路徑變更。

作法:把今天由旗標追加的兩條路徑直接寫進 amp 與 kimi 的 descriptor 讀路徑(home 的 .config/agents/skills 與 XDG 的 agents/skills),寫入路徑一律不動。結果是讀寫行為位元級不變,純重構,不需要任何關於 amp/kimi 是否真的遵守 XDG 的廠商事實。接著刪 descriptor.rs 的 bool 與它的兩個分支、27 行 universal: false、api dto 的欄位與 routes/agents.rs 的填值、重生 ts-rs、descriptor_regression 的那一欄。

同一個 commit 必須做的相依修正(來自 type-first,已驗證且載重):把 .aghub 的兩個 scope 路徑加進 removal::universal_master_roots。它同時餵 allowed_skill_roots(刪除白名單——不加,每次 Master 刪除都會因為 out-of-tree 被拒)與 is_universal_master / single_agent_keep_reason(不加,單一 agent 的刪除會 remove_dir_all 掉 Master)。函式順手改名為 skill_store_roots,因為 .agents/skills 與 ~/.config/agents/skills 現在是共用 Referrer 根、.aghub 才是 Master 根。

api/routes/skills.rs 那段解釋「project .agents/skills 讀者集合是算出來的、因為它會隨 universal: true 移動」的註解要改寫成以讀路徑為準,否則變成假解釋。
judge.q4_rejected:
否決 type-first 把 XDG 半邊當成待決條件丟回來:那會留下一個「實作錯分支就靜默壞掉、測試抓不到」的分叉。安全分支是存在的且不需要廠商事實——保持行為完全不變。

否決 minimal-diff 把 amp/kimi 的 global 寫入路徑改成 get_universal_skills_path():它會把任何已設定 XDG_CONFIG_HOME 的使用者的 Referrer 搬家,理由建立在同一個未驗證的廠商事實上,而且塞在一次本來就很大的重構裡。這是獨立的既有缺口,單獨開一張 issue,不要綁進來。

否決 type-first 把 universal_master_roots 拆成 master_roots + shared_referrer_roots:兩個 consumer 要的是同一個聯集,一份清單就滿足,拆開是為對稱而存在的抽象。

否決 type-first「KeepReason::UniversalMaster 變成不可達、應該刪掉」:已讀碼驗證為假。它是以「包含於 store 根」判定,不是以讀路徑判定;變更後它正是讓單一 agent 刪除不會 remove_dir_all 掉 Master 的那道守衛,必須留著並把 .aghub 納入它的根清單。
new_risks: day-one 破壞:doctor 的 health_of 有 (true, MasterState::Missing) => orphan-lock,而 master_state 只看傳進來的 master_skill。master 一旦指向 .aghub,每個未遷移的 tracked skill 都會被報成 orphan-lock,doctor 的 note 還會叫使用者跑 prune-lock——那會剪掉活的 lock 條目。master_state 必須有 legacy fallback(.agents/skills/<n>),而且要有測試。

Q3 的判準會讓 desktop 的 per-location delete 全面被擋:global 的 codex 原生讀 .agents/skills,若它從未被授權(無私有 Referrer),拿掉共用槽位對它 changed=true,於是它是真受害者;但對話框只送出 location view 列出的 agent,而 load_skills_from_dirs 以名字去重(第一個目錄勝出),codex 可能根本沒被列出。因此 spec 的『discovery 不能再藏起共用 Referrer』從姊妹項升級為 Q3 的前置條件。

崩潰後的 Policy 2 修復會產生兩跳鏈:M 已存在但共用槽位還是實體目錄時,先前建好的私有 Referrer 指向 .agents/skills/<n>,修復把它換成 link 之後那些 Referrer 就變成鏈,被 conformant 的第三個子句判為 violation,該 skill 在重跑 migration 前拒絕 mutation。不是靜默,但必須寫明,而且 migration 的建 Referrer 步驟要對『已經是 link 或已是鏈』冪等。

wire 破壞集中在同一批:SkillCapabilitiesDto.universal、AgentSkillCoverageView 的 reads_master/writes_master/auto_covered 一起消失,AgentInstallResult 多 shared_with。desktop DTO 與 ts-rs 必須同 commit 重生,否則型別對不上只在 typecheck 才爆。
Q3 的拒絕會讓 Non-goals 的地板變成可見的挫折:global 的 cline/warp、project 的 8 個 agent 幾乎無法逐一撤銷授權,使用者必須把所有受害者列進 -a。訊息要直接說明這是 agent 端的限制,否則會變成重複的支援問題。
per-peer 的 read_effect_after 在 project scope 會對同一個共用目錄掃 8 次。行為正確但要以 canonical 目錄去重,否則 delete 的 preview 在大 repo 上會明顯變慢。
leftover 的 .<n>.aghub-migrating 暫時 link 會被 discovery 當成一個指向同一個 Master 的重複條目(名字取自 frontmatter,不是資料夾名)。身分解析後無害,但 resume 必須 unlink 它,且不要讓任何掃描加深到一層以上。
blocking_if_not: master_state 的 legacy fallback 必須與『master 改指向 .aghub』同一個 commit,否則未遷移主機 day-one 全部 orphan-lock 並被建議 prune-lock。
.aghub 的 global 與 project 路徑必須與 universal_canonical_dir 的改動同一個 commit 加進 universal_master_roots(skill_store_roots),兩個 consumer 缺一不可:刪除白名單與 single_agent_keep_reason。
already_linked 的歸屬修正必須與 NativeReader 的刪除同一個 commit。今天它只是重裝時的裝飾性 bug,NativeReader 一刪就變成共用槽位第二個 agent 的首裝 bug:installed: false 且 error: None。created_referrer_dirs 仍只取 install.linked。

Q3 的 helper 必須設 plan.shared_master_kept = true,並在旗標處註明這是第三個生產者(既有兩個:plan_copy_removal 的 UniversalMaster,以及 remove_skill_planned 的 blocks 折疊)。要兩條測試:preview 回 kept 且點名 leftover,--yes 回 unsupported_operation 且 exit 1;把設旗標那行拿掉,preview 會變成 removed/absent 而變紅。
load_skills_from_dirs 的 location view 去重必須先拿掉(或讓拒絕訊息帶出被遮蔽的路徑),否則 desktop 的 per-location delete 會被 Q3 全面擋死。需要一條測試:送出該 location 全部讀者的請求不觸發拒絕。
codex / cursor / opencode 的 global 寫入路徑已驗證為私有(~/.codex/skills、~/.cursor/skills、config/opencode/skills),D3 的主要使用情境成立;project scope 的 codex 寫 .agents/skills,屬於已記載的地板。這條若有人改動 descriptor 必須重驗。
驗收測試第 4 行(home/.agents/skills/<n> 的 symlink_metadata 必須 is_err)要用 CLI harness isolated_cli,並實際 revert 一次看它變紅——其餘各行變更前就會綠。
